query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A combined machine-learned interatomic potential to capture atomic-scale mass and force-constant disorder, coupled with separate Green–Kubo molecular dynamics for phonons and Boltzmann-transport calculations for electrons, will predict the total thermal conductivity of defect-free equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr within ±5% of experiment across 100–1200 K—reducing the average error by ≥15% relative to prior DFT+analytical models.
generation.material_initial_state: Defect-free bulk equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy (<0.1 wt.% oxygen).
generation.intervention: Application of an ML-augmented Green–Kubo MD for lattice heat transport and Boltzmann-transport for electronic conduction.
generation.conditions: Temperature range 100–1200 K; bulk specimens with minimal point defects.
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic mass and force-constant disorder mapping encoded in the ML interatomic potential.
generation.mechanism: Explicit decomposition of thermal conductivity into phononic and electronic contributions via separate simulations.
generation.predicted_outcome: Total thermal conductivity predictions within ±5% of measured values across 100–1200 K; average prediction error ≥15% lower than prior DFT+analytical estimates (which typically err by ±20%).
generation.baseline: Prior DFT-derived analytical conductivity models with ±20% error over the same temperature range.
generation.boundary: Valid for defect-free samples up to 1200 K; not expected to hold for T>1200 K or oxygen contents >1 wt.%.
generation.uncertainty: ±5% due to residual fitting errors in the ML potential; may increase near 100 K and near 1200 K.

falsification_experiment.design: Measure thermal conductivity of high-purity bulk HfNbTaTiZr from 100 K to 1200 K, using 3ω for total conductivity and four-probe electrical measurements plus the Wiedemann–Franz law to separate electronic and lattice components.
measurements: Electrical conductivity vs. T (to infer electronic contribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If predicted total conductivity differs by >±10% from experimental values at two or more temperatures within 100–1200 K, the hypothesis is falsified.
